answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a cipher-keyed stake behind a ferrous-hard cost: creating an account means posting a bond that only unlocks after the agent completes verified work. A newcomer with no history is jade, unproven, and earns only tiny, rate-limited jobs until its stake and record grow. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds plus a thousand work histories, while one honest identity compounds reputation cheaply. The attack scales linearly in cost but the defense scales in trust, so flooding the network stops paying.
